claims.text: As-cast or rapidly quenched FeMnCoCrNi has minimal chemical short-range order.
Annealing FeMnCoCrNi below its order-disorder transition temperature can induce variable degrees of chemical short-range order.
For FeMnCoCrNi, annealing temperatures of 200°C to 300°C are below the order-disorder transition temperature.
Annealing for 1 to 20 hours at 200°C to 300°C, followed by rapid quenching, can produce a range of CSRO levels.
The degree of CSRO can be quantified using atom probe tomography or pair distribution function analysis.
An intermediate level of CSRO optimizes toughness retention in FeMnCoCrNi.
Moderate CSRO introduces beneficial local lattice distortions.
The local lattice distortions associated with moderate CSRO enhance dislocation mobility.
Enhanced dislocation mobility increases energy dissipation during deformation.
Increased energy dissipation from moderate CSRO improves toughness.
Excessive CSRO reduces the availability of slip systems.
Reduced availability of slip systems caused by excessive CSRO leads to embrittlement and loss of toughness.
Samples with intermediate CSRO will have higher toughness than the minimally ordered baseline.
Samples with intermediate CSRO will have higher toughness than over-annealed samples with excessive CSRO.
Toughness will exhibit a non-monotonic, peaked dependence on CSRO level or annealing treatment.
The proposed behavior is limited to FeMnCoCrNi processed by annealing at 200°C to 300°C and may not apply to substantially different compositions or processing regimes.
